KS-2025-HB2692.aiSummary: The bill would set conduct rules for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents in Kansas. It would bar face coverings, require ID and clearly marked vehicles, require judicial search warrants for some searches and raids, and set a minimum training level. KS-2025-HB2679.aiSummary: The bill would create rules for adult-use cannabis in Kansas. It would set up licensing and regulation for growing, making, moving, having, and selling cannabis, and it would set fines and penalties for breaking the rules. KS-2025-HB2651.aiSummary: The bill would change Kansas rules on paternity acknowledgments, which are signed forms that say who a child’s father is. It would let a person challenge one later in cases of fraud, duress, or a material mistake of fact, and it says certain genetic test results count as that kind of mistake. It would also require courts to consider a child’s best interests before ending an acknowledgment in some cases. The act would take effect when published in the statute book.

actions.text: Died in Committee
Referred to House Committee on Commerce, Labor and Economic Development
Introduced

KS-2025-HB2598.aiSummary: The bill would create a paid family leave program in Kansas for covered workers and some self-employed people who choose to join. It would let eligible people take paid leave to bond with a new child, care for a family member with a serious health condition, recover from their own serious health condition, or handle certain military family needs. The program would start paying benefits on July 1, 2027, and would set up a state fund for the leave payments. Employers would also have to give notice and handle payroll deductions for the premium that helps pay for the program.
